concepts.name: Your loving devotion in the morning
concepts.why: Biblical-theological / academic: 'New every morning' is Lam 3:23 only. Ps 59:16, 90:14, 92:2 and 143:8 say loving devotion in the morning and say nothing is new. The phrase from Ps 59:16/92:2/143:8 covers all six passages and Lam 3:22-23 still sits under it (the mercies of loving devotion, each morning).

concepts.name: A parent's compassion for a child
concepts.why: Academic / Jewish reader: the name is Ps 103:13's father, but Isa 49:15 is a mother and nursing child, Jer 31:20 and Hos 11:8 name Ephraim (a son in Jer 31:20 only), and Luke 15:20 is a parable father the text does not name as God. A plain label holds all five without saying who the parable father stands for.

Reformed / Lutheran / academic: Exod 20:6 says loving devotion to 'those who love Me and keep My commandments', not those who fear Him. The name says fear; the other five say fear (Luke 1:50 'fear Him'). Dropping it keeps the name true. It could go under 'I will remember My covenant' (covenant loyalty) if wanted.
Academic: Rom 10:12 shares only the word 'rich' ('gives richly to all who call'); it does not say mercy or compassion. Ps 86:5, Ps 116:5, Eph 2:4 and Jas 5:11 do.

Academic: Lam 3:33 ('He does not willingly afflict') says nothing of the wicked or of death; it belongs under 'Will He be angry forever?' or 'In wrath, remember mercy'. Reformed note, no change required: 1 Tim 2:4 and 2 Pet 3:9 are quoted without gloss and sit beside Rom 9:18 elsewhere, so no side is taken, but keep them unglossed.

note_fixes: Luke 18:14: note 'this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified' has no referent here and puts the weight on 'justified' (Lutheran, Reformed, Catholic, Wesleyan each read it differently); quote the humbling clause instead: 'everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted'
concepts.why: Lutheran / Reformed / Catholic: the concept is contrition and humility, which the second half of the verse says; the 'justified' note makes the passage about something the name does not claim.

concepts.name: Hear and forgive
concepts.why: Academic: 'from heaven' is in 1 Kgs 8:30 and 2 Chr 7:14 only. Num 14:20 (the answer), 1 Kgs 8:50, Dan 9:19 and Amos 7:2 ask or grant forgiveness without it. 'May You hear and forgive' (1 Kgs 8:30) / 'listen... forgive' (Dan 9:19) is what all six say.

concepts.name: Blotted out, whiter than snow
concepts.why: Academic: Ps 51:7 and Isa 1:18 are washing and white-as-snow, not blotting out; Ps 51:9, Isa 44:22 and Acts 3:19 are blotting/wiping away. The name 'Blot out my transgressions' is Ps 51:1 and says more than two of five passages. A name using both images (both in the texts' words) holds all five.

Academic / Lutheran / Reformed: Jas 2:13 is about the mercy a person must show ('anyone who has not been merciful'), not God's mercy in His wrath, so it does not hold 'In wrath, remember mercy'. Move it to the concept on mercy toward others (28). Ps 25:6 has no wrath in it but is the petition to remember His compassion; keep.

Academic / Jewish reader: Matt 23:23 lists mercy among the weightier matters of the law and says nothing of sacrifice; it shares the word 'mercy'. Hos 6:6 and Matt 9:13, 12:7 say 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' in so many words. Move Matt 23:23 to the concept on mercy toward others (28).

concepts.name: Mercy toward one another
note_fixes: add James 2:13 (moved from 23), with its note 'Mercy triumphs over judgment'
concepts.why: Academic: 'Blessed are the merciful' is Matt 5:7 only. Mic 6:8, Zech 7:9, Matt 18:33, Luke 6:36, Luke 10:37 and Col 3:12 do not say blessed. A plain label ('mercy toward one another', from Zech 7:9) holds all, with Matt 5:7 still quoted in full.

concepts.name: A new heart and a new spirit
concepts.why: Lutheran / Reformed / Wesleyan / Catholic: 'I will give you a new heart' is Ezek 36:26, but Ezek 18:31 says 'fashion for yourselves a new heart', Ps 51:10 asks 'Create in me', and Deut 30:6 says 'will circumcise'. Under 'I will give' the grouping takes the monergist side of who makes the heart new, and Ezek 18:31 does not say it. 'A new heart and a new spirit' is the phrase both Ezek 18:31 and 36:26 use and leaves the agent where each text puts it.
Academic: Jer 33:6 ('health and healing') has no faithlessness or sin in the verse; the other four heal sin or apostasy. It belongs under 'He has wounded us, but He will bind up our wounds'.

concepts.name: The remnant of Israel
concepts.why: Baptist (dispensational) / Reformed / academic: 'A remnant will return' is Isa 10:21 and the gatherings, but Rom 9:27 ('only the remnant will be saved') and Rom 11:5 ('a remnant chosen by grace' at the present time) do not say return, so under that name the NT verses read as the same event, which is the Israel-and-church question. 'The remnant of Israel' (Mic 2:12, Zeph 3:13; Rom 9:27 speaks of Israelites) is what all seven say and decides nothing about who the remnant is now.

concepts.name: They went up to Jerusalem to rebuild
concepts.why: Academic: 'They returned to Jerusalem and Judah' is Ezra 2:1 only. Ezra 1:1 and 1:5, 2 Chr 36:23 are the going up, Ezra 3:11, Neh 2:18 and Hag 1:14 are the work after arrival. A name for going up and beginning to rebuild holds all eight in the texts' words ('go up', 'rebuild').

note_fixes: Isa 55:3 does not say king; keep it only if the concept is read as 'David', otherwise move it with Acts 13:34 to the missing sub-theme 'the loving devotion promised to David'
concepts.why: Jewish / Baptist (dispensational) / Reformed / Catholic: Acts 13:34 does not contain 'David their king'; it is Paul's quotation of Isa 55:3 in a sermon about the resurrection, so sitting it under the king David of Jer 30:9, Ezek 34:23, 37:24 and Hos 3:5 tells the reader who that David is, the one thing the drafter says no line does. It fits only a concept built on the shared words 'promised to David'.

note_fixes: add Amos 9:12 ('so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name') beside Acts 15:16-17: Acts 15:17 follows the Greek wording of Amos, which differs from the Hebrew of 9:12, and the Hebrew arbitrates; showing Amos 9:11 without 9:12 lets Acts' words stand for Amos's
concepts.why: Academic / Baptist (dispensational) / Reformed: this is the classic place where the readings part, and setting Acts 15 only against 9:11 gives the reader no way to see the two wordings differ. Adding Amos 9:12 puts the original's words beside James's, which is neutral and lets each reader compare.

Baptist (dispensational) / Reformed / Catholic / Orthodox: Acts 1:6-7 is a question about restoring the kingdom to Israel and a reply that the times are not theirs to know; it does not say the LORD will not abandon His people. Under this name it is made to answer yes (or, read the other way, to be set aside), which is the Israel-and-church question decided by grouping. Rom 11:1, 11:29, Jer 31:37, Ps 94:14, 1 Sam 12:22, Deut 4:31 say the name. Acts 3:21 already stands in 'I make all things new' and the Kingdom link carries Acts 1:6.

secondary_or_links: Secondary 'Restoration -> Renewal' cites Titus 3:5 in full, including 'the washing of new birth', which is read differently on baptism (Lutheran, Catholic, Orthodox, Baptist); the secondary carries no gloss so it takes no side, but the sub-label 'Renewal' should stay as the word of the verse ('renewal by the Holy Spirit') and not be extended.

Concept 25 (You are My people) is accepted: Hos 1:10 and 2:23 are set beside Rom 9:24-25 and 1 Pet 2:10 with the drafter's notes quoting only the verses; keep Hos 2:23's note and the Rom 9:24-25 note exactly as they are, since any paraphrase would say whom Hosea's words belong to.

Links: no change, but the list has no link for a theme on Israel, the land or the nations if the site has one; several concepts (40-45, 50) are about that and a reader leaving from them has no door. Add it only if such a theme exists.

missing.sub_theme: Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven
missing.why: The texts plainly develop forgiveness between people (the prayer, Peter's question, Paul's 'forgiving each other as God forgave you', Joseph and his brothers); the outline has forgiveness only as God's act, and mercy toward others thinly (concept 28). Matt 6:14-15 and 18:35 are the conditional half and belong with it, quoted without gloss.

missing.sub_theme: The fatherless, the widow and the stranger
missing.why: Compassion for the vulnerable is the texts' own picture of the LORD's mercy in action ('for I am compassionate', Exod 22:27) and a reader of this theme would expect it; the outline has God's compassion for the sinner and the exile but not for the poor and powerless.

missing.sub_theme: I will repay you for the years the locust has eaten
missing.why: The drafter left Joel 2:25 unplaced; the texts speak plainly of lost years and harvests restored, a distinct strand from the land and the cities, and it is among the best-known restoration verses.

missing.sub_theme: The loving devotion promised to David
missing.why: Isa 55:3 says 'My loving devotion promised to David' and the texts keep the phrase (2 Sam 7:15; Ps 89); it joins mercy and the Davidic promise by the texts' own word and is the right home for Isa 55:3 and Acts 13:34 if they leave 'David their king'. Acts 13:34 stands beside Isa 55:3 as the same words, with no claim about who.

Optional but honest: the texts also set limits and refusals of pardon, and this theme otherwise leaves them out (the dark in concept 24 is only Israel's judgment). Readers part on eternal security, so quote each verse bare and place it with no gloss; the hope concept then closes the theme as the rule requires.
